utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yesterday I was mentioning to the Prosecution whether they would be prepared to take the motion of the Defence. Are you ready for it this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we can argue the matter today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes. Can we hear -- I think it's Ms. McMurrey's motion, this question of the safe conduct for Defence witnesses. Is that the one we were referring to? Yes. Is that the one were all Mr. Moran's motion --

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It was Mr. Moran's motion. I think we are in a position to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Whatever the Court's pleasure, as far as we are concerned. We can put in another one today, just for logistical reasons, but whatever order the Court wants to do it in, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Either of them, because I didn't think there was any difficulty in dealing with any of them. Which of them are you willing to take on?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We are willing to take whichever ones Your Honours want to do. When Your Honours first raised it, I thought you were talking about the motion by Mr. Moran in relation to Dr. Bellas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That was the one I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we can do that. Although yesterday, from what you were saying, we did not think there was so much in it, except Mr. Moran suggested that there was far more to it than merely hitting a person with a baseball bat. If there is much more than that, then perhaps you might add the addition of reasons why you think he needed a medical doctor for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is considerable evidence of not only beatings throughout the -- from numerous Prosecution witnesses, but also testimony about burnings and other things, plus testimony about conditions in the camp. Now, I agree with Judge Jan that the Court doesn't need an expert to tell it that if someone gets hit 250 times with a baseball bat, he is going to be severely injured. But there are other instances where Prosecution witnesses claimed injuries, and there are other incidents where they claim things occurred involving conditions in the camp. As a forensic pathologist, board certified both in pathology and forensic pathology, Dr. Bellas has the training and experience to interpret some of the testimony that was given, and I believe aid the Court in the credibility of that just by talking about the reasonable medical probability of these things. Just so the Court will know, I've gone through most of the transcript, and I am still going through more, pulling out testimony from the Prosecution witnesses and then delivering it to Dr. Bellas. And I am also going to provide a disk of all that I pull out to the Prosecutor, so nobody is going to be surprised by anything. I think that this could be helpful to the Trial Chamber in judging credibility of some of these witnesses, I say solely based on reasonable medical probability. The registry has informed me unofficially -- verbally that they have no problem with Dr. Bellas appearing. I have not received any written confirmation on that, but I'm sure that that will be coming. I suspect that his testimony will not be so long that it would delay the trial unnecessarily. In fact, given the amount of time that your scheduling order has given me, I suspect I am going to give the Court some time back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Forensic medicine is a very large subject. If you tell us the fields in which he is going to cover, maybe that will be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Well, first, based on his background, of course. Dr. Bellas was the former --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That's all right, but the fields that you want to cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Well, we want to cover things like blunt trauma injury and with specific in testimony. In all reasonable probability, if you were hit across the bottom of the back twice with a board, which is one piece of the testimony, in all reasonable medical probability, given no medical treatment, what would the result of that be. In all reasonable medical probability, if you were in a hot tin building with very -- with limited water, what would the result of that be over a period of months. That type of thing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to join in with Mr. Moran, because I believe this forensic specialist would be helpful also in the Defence of Esad Landzo with regard to the allegations of burns that the Prosecution witnesses have told about. And also we have photographs, we have medical examinations of the witnesses here, and he would be able to relate those as to what it would have been like, or what the probability of those existing in 1992 or prior to 1992. So I believe he would be very helpful to the Defence of Esad Landzo also. So we join in Mr. Moran's request for this forensic psychologist -- psychologist -- this forensic specialist to help us also. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any comments on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, now we know a little more about what this testimony is about. But we object to the calling of Dr. Bellas, and we are submitting to Your Honours that the motion should be denied. We do that for this reason, that we say that the evidence would be, one, cumulative and, B, not the best evidence. And the reason we say that is because all the way through the Prosecution case the opportunity was available to the Defence, and was availed of, to have Prosecution witnesses medically examined. Medical examinations were carried out and reports were filed and submitted to the Court, and they are before the Court. And what the Defence is seeking to do by this motion is to call a witness to comment upon the evidence. And that's all they are doing. Whereas the medical examinations that were carried out is direct evidence and the best evidence, because an examination of the witnesses was done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: We had these photographs on the record. Don't you need an expert to explain those photographs to us?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't have thought so, Your Honours. I would have thought that two things may have been helpful with more information as required. One is for an expert -- the doctors that actually carried out the examinations to come along and to explain, A, why there is an absence of, say, bruising at this stage or whatever, or why there isn't extensive scarring and all of those things. And this would have been very helpful if this -- presumably, if this is the line the Defence wanted to pursue, because these doctors carried out the examination and the witnesses were here. And also they would have been in a position to ask any relevant questions of the witnesses, which may have been assisted in this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) -- did not examine those doctors who took the photograph, therefore, they want to produce a doctor to tell us what those photographs mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But the fact that these witnesses weren't examined is not something that should be -- the medical examination wasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Let them examine the expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, if Your Honours feel -- I am making my submission. I submit that it is inappropriate and it will give rise to the Prosecution having to pursue this matter in rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I didn't think it will be of any value at all. I don't see the value in merely commenting on what another doctor has examined. I don't see -- if you want it as evidence, let him come and say something, but definitely I think it's of very little value, because much of what he will be doing is post facto. The thing has happened, the circumstances have changed, he is merely imagining what the position would have been at that time, and it would not be of any use. If he is one of the doctors who examined the accused persons for burns and the like, that will be direct evidence. Now he would not be doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so it's real clear, we are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you insist on the -- and the registry is prepared to consider that to you, they might do that. But I am only telling you what I feel about the worth of that evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Just so that it's real clear, we are not going to ask Dr. Bellas to comment upon the examinations of the Dutch physicians. What we are going to ask Dr. Bellas to comment on is the likelihood of -- well, given the testimony of the witnesses and the result that the witnesses say occurred because of this blunt trauma, or this other kind of trauma, or the conditions in the camp, what the medical probability would be of a given result. Your Honour, if the Trial Chamber is going to allow them to appear, I would ask one thing, to try to save everybody a little bit of time and money, that we pick a date certain per chance -- I would suggest the Wednesday, the 8th of July, to have him appear here no matter what else is happening. That's in the middle of the time the Court has set aside. If we finish the rest of our case, bring him in on that day, or if there is another witness. Just because it's probably more economical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I will consider that. You say it's evidence, you tender your evidence, but it doesn't mean much to what, perhaps, we have seen and heard and observed the witnesses themselves. I don't now whatever opinion he would be giving us without even seeing any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think we will grant it. We'll grant it, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will have him here on that Wednesday, then. And, in fact, I will have him here a few days early, if the Prosecutor wants to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, we might be able -- if he can have them to change their views. Are you -- I think we'll take this other question of the safe conduct application thing. I think that is Ms. McMurrey's application, the safe conduct of some of the witnesses. I think one of them, is it? One witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The safe conduct has a confidential annex, and that's why I believe that maybe we should go into private session at this point to discuss this.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
